prize_parts.citation: for the invention and realisation of optical lattice clocks based on magic-wavelength trapping, bringing atomic clocks to the 10^-18 level

statement.case_for: After reading all eight openings I move my preferred configuration to the optical lattice clock. It is the only candidate that every colleague independently ranked, and the support comes from people with different instincts: Kroll and Lindroth first, Johansson second, Pearce third. The case fits what I understand the prize to be for: an invention (magic-wavelength trapping, proposed and first demonstrated by Katori) that opens a door, because it makes frequency differences at the 10^-18 level, or height differences of millimetres, observable. It has been reproduced and compared across many laboratories (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE and others), so verification is not in question, and the two-name attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist. My own first choice, aberration-corrected electron microscopy (B011), is, on the evidence I know, as original an invention as any here, but only I ranked it, and I should not read my own expertise as scientific merit that colleagues can be expected to share. I therefore keep it as an alternative and ask that colleagues look at it properly, instead of dropping it because it is outside their fields.
statement.case_against: My main reservation is the one the statutes make me press: the prize is for the original experiment, not for the second discoverer who did it much better. Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice and demonstrated the first Sr lattice clock, so his credit is on the original work. Ye's strongest contribution is bringing the clock to record accuracy and stability, which is a very large achievement but could be described as improving a technique rather than discovering it. If the committee cannot show that Ye's own contributions (independent Sr lattice work at JILA, the link to frequency combs, many-body operation) are original and decisive, a Katori-only or differently composed citation would be more defensible. A second concern is overlap with the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 ion-trap prize, and the risk that this is read as precision engineering rather than discovery. The redefinition of the second has not happened, which does not affect scientific merit but may matter to how the prize is understood.

responses.point: Optical lattice clocks are the clearest case of a new measurement technique changing what can be observed, with high originality, clarity and breadth of consequence, in the tradition of the 2005 comb prize and the 1989 and 2012 precision-spectroscopy prizes.
responses.response: I agree with the principle and it is why I have moved toward this candidate: a new tool that lets us see something we could not see before is the kind of door I want to credit. I would qualify the framing. Tradition is not a reason in itself, and the earlier precision-spectroscopy prizes make us ask what is new in the lattice clock beyond better numbers. My answer is the magic-wavelength trapping idea, which removes the dominant systematic and is a genuine invention. I would like the citation to state that concept explicitly, and I would like the record to establish that the Sr lattice demonstration, and not only later improvements, supports the named priority for both laureates.

responses.point: The experimental observation of the Higgs boson at ATLAS and CMS is the most important discovery in particle physics of the century, still unrecognised on the experimental side, with Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee as founding leaders.
responses.response: I ranked B010 second and share the view that the experimental discovery is overdue; the 2013 prize went to the prediction. On attribution I disagree with the opening framing. You acknowledge that the three are founders and detector leaders and that the decisive contributions are distributed, and I read that as a serious problem under our rules, not just a drafting issue. The statutes ask us to identify the people who did the original work. Leadership of a proposal is not equal to making the discovery, and the people who made the 2012 observation (analysis leaders, spokespersons in 2012, trigger and detector builders) are not on the list. Until we can say who the right three are and why, I cannot put B010 first, however strong the science. If you can make the case for the founders as the originators of the experiments as instruments, I will listen, but I want that argued explicitly.

responses.point: Twisted bilayer graphene (B024) is the clean model-meets-experiment pattern, a predicted flat-band mechanism followed by an experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity, and it created an entire field; B021 follows close behind.
responses.response: I accept the pattern and the importance of the field, and I take seriously that you rank it first. My difficulty is maturity and verification. Eight years after the experiments, the pairing mechanism is unresolved and sample-to-sample variability is large, and you note yourself that the superconductivity mechanism is not settled. Our standard is that the result be experimentally verified and the topic and people be identified with certainty. I think the correlated insulator and superconducting phases are real, but I am not yet sure how a citation should be worded, or whether Cao, as first author of the 2018 experiments, should be credited. I would rather this be left for a later year than be rushed. On B021 I also share your concern about Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang; Zhang is deceased, which constrains attribution, and I do not see how Kane, Mele and Molenkamp alone can be called complete.

responses.point: Katori's magic-wavelength lattice idea and Ye's realisation turned atomic spectroscopy into the most precise measurement ever made; two laureates give a natural and fair configuration, and the result is clean, original and easy to explain.
responses.response: I largely agree and this is the central reason I now prefer B052. I would add one caution to your attribution point. You describe Katori as proposing and Ye as realising, and the second part of that is where the rule about the original experiment applies most directly. Ludlow, Hinkley, Bloom and others did a great deal of the JILA work that took the accuracy to the record levels, and the committee should be satisfied about which part of the clock achievement is Ye's own. I also ask whether your comfort that the 2005 and 2012 prizes do not interfere is based on the specific record of who invented what, or on the general impression that this is a different thing. I have not seen the details either, so I treat this as an open question.

uncertainties: Whether Ye's contribution to the lattice clock is an original and decisive step, or an improvement of Katori's invention to record accuracy.

How much of the lattice-clock priority record (Katori's proposal and first Sr demonstration versus early experiments from other groups such as Lemonde, Lisdat and Ludlow) I have verified; I am relying on memory.
Whether three or fewer individuals can honestly represent the Higgs discovery (B010), which is why I cannot support it first.
Whether the STEM aberration-corrector work (Krivanek and collaborators) weakens the Rose, Urban and Haider attribution for B011, since the supplied credit list does not include it.
Whether the committee will treat aberration-corrected electron microscopy as a discovery or invention in the statutory sense, or as an enabling instrument, given that it was ranked by me alone.
statement.conflict_note: B011 (aberration-corrected electron microscopy) is in my own research field, transmission electron microscopy, and I am President of the International Federation of Societies for Microscopy, so a perception of bias toward B011 is possible and the committee may wish to weigh my advocacy accordingly or consider recusal on that ballot. My profile does not show a direct personal tie to Rose, Urban or Haider, nor to any candidate on the shortlist. Goran Johansson is a colleague in Chalmers Physics, which is relevant to B056 (his own field) but not a conflict for my preferred B052.
